# Sameer Saurav

> Computational chemist and Assistant Professor of Chemistry at A.N.S. College, Nabinagar, Bihar, India. Ph.D. from IIT Kanpur; BS-MS in Chemical Sciences from IISER Kolkata. Works on molecular dynamics, enhanced sampling, free energy calculations and reaction-rate theory. Writes essays and explainers on chemistry, education and everyday life. Open to commissions for explainers, op-eds and features.

- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sameer-saurav/
- X: https://x.com/Sameerchm
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0002-0281-1977

## Pages

- [Home](https://sameersaurav.github.io/): introduction and contact
- [Writing](https://sameersaurav.github.io/writing.html): essays, explainers and published articles
- [Publications](https://sameersaurav.github.io/publications.html): peer-reviewed research papers

## Key facts

- Ph.D., IIT Kanpur (2026), thesis on kinetics from sliced sampling approaches.
- BS-MS in Chemical Sciences, IISER Kolkata.
- Trained at BARC Training School (IGCAR, Kalpakkam); Scientific Officer at Tarapur Atomic Power Station 3&4.
- Teaching at A.N.S. College, Nabinagar, since 2017.
- Articles published in The India Forum, Swarajya, Research Matters and IndiaBioscience, among others.

## Writing on this site

- [The Blue That Brought Gandhi to Bihar](https://sameersaurav.github.io/writing/champaran-indigo.html): Gandhi's first satyagraha in India was fought over indigo. A chemist's look at the dye, the vats of Champaran and the German laboratory that changed the story.
- [Thekua, Diyas and the Setting Sun: The Chemistry of Chhath](https://sameersaurav.github.io/writing/chhath-chemistry.html): Thekua browning in the kadhai, a ghee diya on the ghat, the red sun over the river: a chemist's look at Chhath.
- [Why Is Blue So Rare in the Diwali Sky?](https://sameersaurav.github.io/writing/diwali-blue.html): Diyas, flame colours, phuljhadi sparks and the rare blue firework: a chemist's look at the light of Diwali.
- [Made to Return: How Durga Idols Are Built to Go Back to the River](https://sameersaurav.github.io/writing/durga-idol-clay.html): Durga idols are made from riverbank clay and go back to the river after the festival. A chemist's look at why the old way of making them works so well.
- [Book Review: May Contain Lies by Alex Edmans](https://sameersaurav.github.io/writing/may-contain-lies-review.html): A review of Alex Edmans's May Contain Lies, on why intelligent people believe things that aren't true.
- [Patna, Turn It Down a Little](https://sameersaurav.github.io/writing/patna-noise.html): DJ trucks, pressure horns and what all that noise does to us. A look at why Patna is so loud, and how we might turn it down a little.
